blocks.text: Aaj ka sabaq bohat practical hai. Pichle topics mein hum ne lines ki equations banayi thin; ab sawal yeh hai ke jab do lines ek doosre ko kaat-ti hain to un ke darmiyan angle kitna hota hai? Socha jaye to har cheez slope mein chhupi hui hai, kyunke slope hi batata hai ke line kitni jhuki hui hai. Is sabaq ke aakhir tak aap sirf do slopes dekh kar angle bata sakenge, aur kisi bhi triangle ke teeno angles nikal sakenge.

Kitab kehti hai: maan lijiye \(\ell_1\) aur \(\ell_2\) do aisi lines hain jo ek doosre ko kaat-ti hain \((\ell_1 \nparallel \ell_2)\), yani parallel nahi hain, aur point \(P\) par milti hain. Point \(P\) par yeh dono lines do supplementary angles (aise do angles jin ka jama \(180^\circ\) ho) banati hain.

Agar \(\ell_1 \perp \ell_2\) na hon (yani dono ke darmiyan theek \(90^\circ\) na ho), to in do angles mein se ek zaroor acute (\(90^\circ\) se chhota) hoga. Ab ahem definition: \(\ell_1\) se \(\ell_2\) tak ka angle woh angle \(\theta\) hai jitna \(\ell_1\) ko point \(P\) ke gird counterclockwise (ghari ki suiyon ke ulat) ghumaya jaye ke woh \(\ell_2\) par aa kar baith jaye.

Neeche wali figure mein \(\theta\) hi angle of intersection hai. Yeh bhi yaad rahe ke kisi line ki inclination (jhukaao ka angle) woh angle hai jo positive \(x\)-axis se line tak counterclockwise direction mein naapa jaye.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is ko yun samjhiye: do lines kaat-ti hain to \(P\) par do angles bante hain, maslan \(60^\circ\) aur \(120^\circ\). In ka jama hamesha \(180^\circ\) hota hai. Ab kaun sa angle hum maangte hain? Is uljhan ko khatam karne ke liye kitab ne direction fix kar di: \(\ell_1\) par khare ho jaiye aur ghari ki suiyon ke ulat ghoomiye, jab tak \(\ell_2\) par na pohanch jayein. Jitna ghoome, wohi '\(\ell_1\) se \(\ell_2\) tak' ka angle hai.
Misaal: darwaza kholte waqt aap kehte hain 'darwaza deewar se \(30^\circ\) khula'; yahan bhi shuruat ek line se hoti hai aur ghoom kar doosri tak jate hain.
Agar aap \(\ell_2\) se shuru karein to doosra angle milega: \(\ell_2\) se \(\ell_1\) tak ka angle \(180^\circ - \theta\) hai. Is liye lines ka order bohat ahem hai.
Yaad karein (5.1): line ka slope \(m = \tan\alpha\) hota hai, jahan \(\alpha\) us ki inclination hai (\(0^\circ \le \alpha < 180^\circ\)).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar do lines ke darmiyan ek angle \(70^\circ\) hai to doosra angle kitna hoga? (Jawab: \(110^\circ\), kyunke dono supplementary hain.)
Theorem 7

Theorem ka matlab hai ek aisi baat jo hum saabit (prove) karenge. Kitab kehti hai: maan lijiye \(\ell_1\) aur \(\ell_2\) do non-vertical lines (khari seedhi nahi) hain jo ek doosre par perpendicular bhi nahi. Agar \(m_1\) aur \(m_2\) in ke slopes hain, to \(\ell_1\) se \(\ell_2\) tak ka angle \(\theta\) yeh formula deta hai:

blocks.text_alt: tan theta equals m2 minus m1, over 1 plus m1 m2

blocks.text: Yeh formula kyun aur kab? Jab bhi do lines ke slopes maloom hon (ya points se nikal sakte hon) aur un ke darmiyan angle chahiye, yahi formula lagta hai. Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: upar 'jis line ki taraf ghoom rahe ho us ka slope pehle', yani \(m_2 - m_1\).
Proof

Proof shuru karne se pehle idea samajh lein: har line ka apna jhukaao (inclination) hota hai, \(\ell_1\) ka \(\alpha_1\) aur \(\ell_2\) ka \(\alpha_2\). Dono ko positive \(x\)-axis se naapa jata hai. To dono lines ke darmiyan ka angle bas in do jhukaaon ka farq hona chahiye. Phir \(\tan\) lene se jhukaao slopes mein badal jate hain, aur formula tayyar.

Figure 5.8 ko dhyan se dekhiye. Is mein se hum yeh relation parhte hain:
\[\alpha_2 = \alpha_1 + \theta\]
ya
\[\theta = \alpha_2 - \alpha_1\]
Ab dono taraf \(\tan\) lete hain:
\[\tan\theta = \tan(\alpha_2 - \alpha_1)\]
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{\tan\alpha_2 - \tan\alpha_1}{1 + \tan\alpha_1\tan\alpha_2}\]
Aur kyunke \(\tan\alpha_1 = m_1\), \(\tan\alpha_2 = m_2\):
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1 m_2}\]

A green line l2 falls to the right and meets the x-axis at the obtuse angle alpha 2. The lines cross at P, where an arc marks the angle theta turning anticlockwise from l1 to l2.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Pehli line \(\alpha_2 = \alpha_1 + \theta\) kahan se aayi? Figure mein dono lines aur \(x\)-axis mil kar ek triangle banate hain. \(\alpha_2\) is triangle ka exterior angle (bahar wala angle) hai, aur geometry ka purana rule hai ke exterior angle saamne ke do interior angles ke jama ke barabar hota hai, yahan \(\alpha_1\) aur \(\theta\).
Phir humne \(\tan(A - B) = \frac{\tan A - \tan B}{1 + \tan A\tan B}\) wala formula lagaya jo aap Class XI ki trigonometry mein parh chuke hain, aur \(\tan\) ki jagah slope rakh diya.
Shartein kyun? Vertical line ka slope hota hi nahi (\(\tan 90^\circ\) defined nahi), is liye \(m\) use nahi ho sakta. Aur agar lines perpendicular hon to \(1 + m_1 m_2 = 0\) ho jata hai aur fraction ki koi value nahi rehti; yeh Corollary 2 mein dekhenge.
Corollary 1

Corollary ka matlab hai theorem se seedha nikalne wala natija. \(\ell_1 \parallel \ell_2\) agar aur sirf agar \(m_1 = m_2\). Kyunke \(\ell_1 \parallel \ell_2\) hon to \(\theta = 0\), is liye
\[\Leftrightarrow \tan\theta = 0 = \dfrac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1 m_2}\]
\[\Leftrightarrow m_2 = m_1\]
Fraction tab zero hota hai jab us ka numerator zero ho; is liye \(m_2 - m_1 = 0\). Seedhi baat: parallel lines ka jhukaao ek jaisa hota hai.
Corollary 2

\(\ell_1 \perp \ell_2\) agar aur sirf agar \(1 + m_1 m_2 = 0\). Kyunke \(\ell_1 \perp \ell_2\) hon to \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}\), is liye
\[\Leftrightarrow \tan\dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1 m_2} = \infty\]
\[\Leftrightarrow \infty = \dfrac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1 m_2}\]
kitab ke box mein likha hai: \(\because \tan\frac{\pi}{2} = \infty\)
\[\Leftrightarrow 1 + m_1 m_2 = 0\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Asal mein \(\tan 90^\circ\) koi number nahi, yeh undefined hai. Kitab ke \(\infty\) ka matlab hai: jab \(\theta\) \(90^\circ\) ke qareeb jata hai to \(\tan\theta\) beghair kisi had ke barhta hai. Koi fraction beghair had ke tab hi barhta hai jab us ka denominator zero ki taraf jaye; isi liye \(1 + m_1 m_2 = 0\).
Saaf tareeqa: \(\theta = 90^\circ\) tab hota hai jab \(\cot\theta = 0\), aur \(\cot\theta = \frac{1 + m_1 m_2}{m_2 - m_1}\). Yeh zero tab hai jab \(1 + m_1 m_2 = 0\), yani \(m_1 m_2 = -1\).
Khulasa: parallel lines ke slopes barabar; perpendicular lines ke slopes ka product \(-1\). Misaal: slope 2 wali line par perpendicular line ka slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\) hoga.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text:
Formula \(\tan\theta = \frac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1 m_2}\) lagane ka tareeqa:
1. Pehle tay karein ke kis line se ghoom rahe hain (\(m_1\)) aur kis tak (\(m_2\)). Jis tak ghoomna hai us ka slope numerator mein pehle.
2. Agar \(\tan\theta > 0\) aaye to \(\theta\) acute hai: \(\theta = \tan^{-1}(\tan\theta)\).
3. Agar \(\tan\theta < 0\) aaye to \(\theta\) obtuse hai: \(\theta = 180^\circ - \tan^{-1}|\tan\theta|\). Calculator negative angle de to \(180^\circ\) jama karein.
4. Lines ke darmiyan acute angle hamesha \(\tan^{-1}\left|\frac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1 m_2}\right|\) hota hai.
Ab kitab ki do misaalein karte hain. Pehli mein seedha formula lagega, doosri mein triangle ke teeno angles nikalenge.

Har sawal se pehle teen cheezein apne aap se poochiye: (1) slopes diye hue hain ya points se nikalne honge? (2) kis line se ghoomna hai aur kis tak, yani \(m_1\) kaun aur \(m_2\) kaun? (3) tan ka jawab positive aaya ya negative, yani angle acute hai ya obtuse? In teen sawalon ke jawab saaf hon to yeh topic bilkul aasaan ho jata hai, aur zyada tar bachon ki ghaltiyan isi teesre qadam par hoti hain.

blocks.title: Example 12
blocks.problem: Find the angle from the line with slope \(-\frac{7}{3}\) to the line with slope \(\frac{5}{2}\).
steps:
Diya gaya: pehli line ka slope \(m_1 = -\frac{7}{3}\), doosri line ka slope \(m_2 = \frac{5}{2}\).
Maloom karna: pehli line se doosri line tak ka angle \(\theta\).
Tareeqa: Theorem 7, \(\tan\theta = \frac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1 m_2}\). Sawal mein 'from' wali line ka slope \(m_1\) aur 'to' wali line ka slope \(m_2\) banega; yahi order sab se ahem hai.

Qadam 1: numerator
\[m_2 - m_1 = \dfrac{5}{2} - \left(-\dfrac{7}{3}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{15 + 14}{6} = \dfrac{29}{6}\]
Kyun: negative ko minus karna jama karne ke barabar hai. 2 aur 3 ka common denominator 6 hai, is liye \(\frac{5}{2} = \frac{15}{6}\) aur \(\frac{7}{3} = \frac{14}{6}\).
Dhyan dein: \(-\left(-\frac{7}{3}\right)\) ko \(-\frac{7}{3}\) likh dena bohat aam ghalti hai; bracket zaroor lagayein.

Qadam 2: denominator
\[1 + m_1 m_2 = 1 + \left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{7}{3}\right)\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{35}{6} = -\dfrac{29}{6}\]
Kyun: positive aur negative ka product negative hota hai. \(1 = \frac{6}{6}\) likh kar \(\frac{6 - 35}{6} = -\frac{29}{6}\).

Qadam 3: divide karein
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{29/6}{-29/6} = \dfrac{29}{-29} = -1\]
\[\Rightarrow \tan\theta = -1\]
Kyun: upar neeche dono mein 6 hai, cancel ho gaya; kitab bhi yahi karti hai.

Qadam 4: angle parhein
\[\theta = 180^\circ - 45^\circ\]
\[\theta = 135^\circ\]
Kyun: \(\tan 45^\circ = 1\). Tan negative aaya, matlab angle obtuse hai (\(90^\circ\) aur \(180^\circ\) ke darmiyan), is liye \(180^\circ\) mein se \(45^\circ\) minus kiya.
Dhyan dein: calculator \(\tan^{-1}(-1) = -45^\circ\) dega; is mein \(180^\circ\) jama karein to \(135^\circ\) milta hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[\tan 135^\circ = -\tan 45^\circ = -1 \;\checkmark\]
Dono lines ke darmiyan acute angle \(45^\circ\) hai aur \(45^\circ + 135^\circ = 180^\circ\), jaisa supplementary angles mein hona chahiye.

blocks.text: Doosri misaal mein ek triangle hai. Triangle ke har kone (vertex) par do sides milti hain, aur un do sides ke darmiyan wala angle hi interior angle hai. Asal kaam yeh hai ke har kone par tay karein ke kis side se ghoom kar kis side tak jana hai. Asaan rule: triangle ke vertices ko anticlockwise (ghari ki suiyon ke ulat) chakkar mein dekhiye; har vertex par us side se shuru karein jo agle vertex ki taraf jati hai, aur us side tak ghoomein jo pichhle vertex ki taraf jati hai. Is tarah har angle andar ki taraf naapa jata hai aur sahi interior angle milta hai.

blocks.title: Example 13
blocks.problem: Find the angles of the triangle whose vertices are \(A(1, 2)\), \(B(7, 3)\) and \(C(4, 9)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(A(1, 2)\), \(B(7, 3)\), \(C(4, 9)\).
Maloom karna: triangle ke angles \(A\), \(B\), \(C\).
Tareeqa: pehle teeno sides ke slopes, phir har vertex par Theorem 7. Figure 5.9 mein \(A \to B \to C\) anticlockwise chalte hain, is liye har interior angle anticlockwise naapa jata hai: \(A\) par \(AB\) se \(AC\) tak, \(B\) par \(BC\) se \(BA\) tak, \(C\) par \(CA\) se \(CB\) tak.

Qadam 1: sides ke slopes
\(AB\), \(BC\), \(CA\) ke slopes ko \(m_c\), \(m_a\), \(m_b\) kehte hain (har side ka naam saamne wale vertex se: \(a = BC\), \(b = CA\), \(c = AB\)).
\[m_a = \dfrac{9 - 3}{4 - 7} = \dfrac{6}{-3} = -2\]
\[m_b = \dfrac{2 - 9}{1 - 4} = \dfrac{-7}{-3} = \dfrac{7}{3}\]
\[m_c = \dfrac{3 - 2}{7 - 1} = \dfrac{1}{6}\]
Kyun: har side ke do end points se slope \(= \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\).

Qadam 2: angle \(A\), \(\overline{AB}\) se \(\overline{AC}\) tak
Hum \(AB\) (slope \(m_c\)) se ghoom kar \(AC\) (slope \(m_b\)) tak jate hain, is liye \(m_b\) pehle aayega:
\[\tan A = \dfrac{m_b - m_c}{1 + m_b m_c}\]
\[= \dfrac{\frac{7}{3} - \frac{1}{6}}{1 + \left(\frac{7}{3}\right)\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)}\]
\[= \dfrac{13/6}{25/18} = \dfrac{39}{25}\]
\[\Rightarrow A = 57.34^\circ\]
Kyun: \(\frac{7}{3} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{14 - 1}{6} = \frac{13}{6}\) aur \(1 + \frac{7}{18} = \frac{25}{18}\). Phir \(\frac{13}{6} \times \frac{18}{25} = \frac{39}{25}\).
Dhyan dein: kitab ne yahan order ulta likha hai aur \(-\frac{39}{25}\) aaya; neeche 'Kitab ki ghalti' dekhiye.

Qadam 3: angle \(B\), \(\overline{BC}\) se \(\overline{AB}\) tak
\[\tan B = \dfrac{m_c - m_a}{1 + m_c m_a}\]
\[= \dfrac{\frac{1}{6} - (-2)}{1 + \left(\frac{1}{6}\right)(-2)}\]
\[= \dfrac{13/6}{4/6} = \dfrac{13}{4}\]
\[\Rightarrow B = 72.90^\circ\]
Kyun: \(BC\) (slope \(m_a\)) se \(BA\) (slope \(m_c\)) tak ghoomte hain, is liye \(m_c\) pehle; kitab ne yahan order theek likha hai. \(\frac{1}{6} + 2 = \frac{13}{6}\) aur \(1 - \frac{2}{6} = \frac{4}{6}\).

Qadam 4: angle \(C\), \(\overline{AC}\) se \(\overline{BC}\) tak
\[\tan C = \dfrac{m_a - m_b}{1 + m_a m_b}\]
\[= \dfrac{-2 - \frac{7}{3}}{1 + (-2)\left(\frac{7}{3}\right)}\]
\[= \dfrac{-13/3}{-11/3} = \dfrac{13}{11}\]
\[\Rightarrow C = 49.76^\circ\]
Kyun: \(CA\) (slope \(m_b\)) se \(CB\) (slope \(m_a\)) tak, is liye \(m_a\) pehle. Upar neeche dono negative, is liye jawab positive aur angle acute.

Tasdeeq:
\[57.34^\circ + 72.90^\circ + 49.76^\circ = 180^\circ \;\checkmark\]
Teeno tan positive aaye, yani teeno angles acute hain, aur Figure 5.9 mein bhi triangle aisa hi dikhta hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Example 13 mein kitab kehti hai ke angle \(A\) ko \(AB\) se \(AC\) tak naapa jata hai, magar likhti hai \(\tan A = \frac{m_c - m_b}{1 + m_c m_b} = -\frac{39}{25}\). Yeh order \(AC\) se \(AB\) tak ka angle deta hai (\(122.66^\circ\)). Sahi line: \(\tan A = \frac{m_b - m_c}{1 + m_b m_c} = \frac{39}{25}\), is liye \(A = 57.34^\circ\).
Kitab ke decimals bhi thore se hate hue hain: \(\tan^{-1}\frac{39}{25} = 57.34^\circ\) (kitab \(57.35^\circ\)), \(\tan^{-1}\frac{13}{4} = 72.90^\circ\) (kitab \(72.87^\circ\)), \(\tan^{-1}\frac{13}{11} = 49.76^\circ\) (kitab \(49.78^\circ\)). Dono sets ka jama \(180^\circ\) hai, is liye farq sirf rounding ka hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahi.) Line \(y = 2x + 1\) se line \(y = -3x + 4\) tak ka angle nikaliye.
\(m_1 = 2\), \(m_2 = -3\).
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{-3 - 2}{1 + (2)(-3)} = \dfrac{-5}{-5} = 1\]
is liye \(\theta = 45^\circ\). Agar ulta, doosri line se pehli tak, poocha jata to \(\tan\theta = \frac{2 - (-3)}{1 - 6} = -1\) aur \(\theta = 135^\circ\). Dekha? Order badla to jawab \(180^\circ - 45^\circ\) ho gaya.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Slopes \(\frac{2}{3}\) aur \(-\frac{3}{2}\) wali lines ke darmiyan angle kitna hai, formula lagaye beghair? (Ishara: dono ka product dekhiye. Product \(-1\) hai, is liye \(90^\circ\).)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\ell_1\) se \(\ell_2\) tak ka angle woh anticlockwise ghoomna hai jo \(\ell_1\) ko \(\ell_2\) par la de.
2. Theorem 7: \(\tan\theta = \frac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1 m_2}\); \(m_2\) us line ka slope jis tak ghoomna hai.
3. Parallel: \(m_1 = m_2\). Perpendicular: \(m_1 m_2 = -1\).
4. \(\tan\theta\) negative ho to angle obtuse: \(\theta = 180^\circ - \tan^{-1}|\tan\theta|\).
5. Triangle mein vertices ko anticlockwise ghoomein aur har angle 'agle vertex wali side' se 'pichhle vertex wali side' tak naapein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(m_1\) aur \(m_2\) ki jagah badal dena: is se \(\theta\) ki jagah \(180^\circ - \theta\) aata hai (yahi ghalti kitab ke Example 13 mein hai).
2. Calculator se negative angle likh dena: \(\tan^{-1}\) negative de to \(180^\circ\) jama karein.
3. Jab \(1 + m_1 m_2 = 0\) ho to formula mein zero se divide karne ki koshish: is surat mein lines seedhi perpendicular hain, \(\theta = 90^\circ\).
4. Vertical line ka slope lagane ki koshish: us ka slope hota hi nahi, inclination \(90^\circ\) hai; is liye inclinations se kaam karein.
